faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. Use our timesheet to calculate automatically.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the national minimum wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). On our timesheet, you can check a box to add casual loading to your base rate.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my salary?
faqs.a: The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For example, on a $60,000 annual salary, super would be $7,200 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. The super is not deducted from your take-home pay; it is additional.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

Understanding your annual pay from an hourly rate is essential for budgeting, comparing job offers, and planning for tax and super. Whether you are on the national minimum wage, an award rate, or a higher salary like the average NRL salary, the same conversion applies: multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours and then by 52 weeks. This article explains the process, distinguishes between different pay types, and shows how tax and super affect your take-home pay.

## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

Most full-time employees work 38 hours per week, as set by the National Employment Standards. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. For example, a casual employee working 20 hours per week would use 20 hours. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool assumes 38 hours unless you change it.

To find your fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the national minimum wage, weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is $2,009.80 before tax.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This is the base rate for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most employees are covered by a modern award, which sets higher minimum rates for their industry or occupation. Award rates often include penalty rates for weekends, overtime, and allowances. Casual employees receive a 25% loading of 25% on top of the base rate. On our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) checkbox adds that 25% automatically.

## Average Earnings Context: The Average NRL Salary

The average NRL salary is a topic of interest for sports fans and recruiters, but the Fair Work Commission and Australian Bureau of Statistics do not publish a precise figure for NRL salaries. According to the ABS Average Weekly Earnings, May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings are $2,083.70 per week (all employees total earnings $1,579.20 per week). The average NRL salary is generally higher than the national minimum wage, but no official source is not available from official sources. For high-paying professions, the conversion formula still applies: a hypothetical $50 per hour equals $98,800 per year (38 hours × 52 weeks).

## Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is taxed using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Additionally, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For 2025–26, the single reduction thresholds apply (used here as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For example, on a $60,000 annual salary, tax is $4,020 + 30% × ($60,000 – $45,000) = $8,520, plus Medicare $1,200, total $9,720. Your take-home pay would be $50,280 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a detailed estimate.

## Superannuation

Employers must pay super guarantee of 12% on ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay; it is additional. For a $60,000 salary, super is $7,200 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is paid on top of your annual gross pay, so your total employment cost is higher. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

## Conclusion

Converting your hourly rate to annual pay is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. Whether you are on the national minimum wage, an award rate, or a high salary like the average NRL salary, the same formula applies. Use our timesheet to calculate your annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, including casual loading, and see estimated tax and super. Remember that this is an estimate; your actual pay may vary based on overtime, allowances, and salary sacrifice.
